items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I later wrote for Dizzy and I played in Dizzy’s band. I played in Dizzy’s band in 1950.

ctx.x: So Sweet – Sweets Edison asked Snooky, said, “You gon’ – You gonna leave Count Basie’s band to join Gerald Wilson’s band?” Snooky said, “Yeah” [Laughs] So Snooky joins my band and we – but we had a going – by the way, I’m sorry I don’t have the first records we made at that time, and you’ll see why I said that, because my band was powerful. We were – I was the first band to actually record Dizzy Gillespie’s Groovin High…

items.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Dizzy Gillespie had played in his band. They were a very good band.

ctx.x: Listen, you know, we were in Les Hite’s band, which he had a good band. You must remember Les Hite had been to New York City already. He had Gil Fuller writing for him. Dizzy Gillespie had played in his band. They were a very good band. So when I joined him and Snooky came out and he didn’t want to play with the small group, Les Hite says, “we’ll take Snooky on with us.” Well after we left Les Hite’s band, Benny © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

Carter needed a trumpet player so he called me, and he says, “Gerald, I want you to join my band.” I knew Benny from New York, I used to talk with him all the time, and go around and hear his band rehearse over on Lenox. And I had seen his band that he brought to California at that time, and I says, “well Benny, I’ll tell you what, you need one trumpet player, why don’t I just bring you four trumpet players?”
